findings.description: `reschedule` acquires the lock but has no try/finally. When the job is unknown or not PENDING it returns False at line 77 without releasing the lock. The `threading.Lock` stays held forever, so every later call to add/claim_due/finish/get blocks until the timeout and then raises SchedulerBusy. The scheduler is effectively dead after one such call. Any exception raised between acquire and release (e.g. in `replace`) would cause the same problem.
findings.suggestion:
Wrap the body in try/finally and release in the finally block, as the other methods do:

self._acquire()
try:
    job = self._jobs.get(job_id)
    if job is None or job.status is not JobStatus.PENDING:
        return False
    self._jobs[job_id] = replace(job, run_at=run_at)
    return True
finally:
    self._lock.release()
findings.title: Lock not released on early return in reschedule
